races.name: Sticky Toffee Pudding Juvenile Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Vietnorm
runners_data.note: The most naturally credentialed finisher in the race, with back-to-back wins on Good ground and a legitimate hold-up style that is not redistributed here; the 36-day break looks routine for Keatley and Oakley Brown has winning experience — the concern is whether Cartmel's tight flat track gives enough time to produce the finish after a controlled pace.|
runners_data.comment: Vietnorm shaped with real promise when runner-up last time out, and a winner two starts back, so he arrives in fine nick off a 36-day break; the chief concern is whether 159 lb tests his resolve under pressure.

runners_data.name: Wicksey
runners_data.note: The race pivots around her — a confirmed front-runner who won last time out and carries Ben Haslam's decent 14-day form (2/11); the 63-day absence is worth noting but her jumping technique is the key asset on this track, and with no rivals to push her early she can set exactly the fractions she wants.|
runners_data.comment: Wicksey heads this six-runner field on a rating of 96 and arrives on the back of a win last time out, with experience over today's trip adding to his claims; the 63-day absence is the sole query, but the form reads well.

runners_data.name: Jambearee
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison sends this one back after 86 days with a warning flag for fading in the finish — the horse is a natural hold-up type shifted into the midfield map because the rear is overcrowded, and a pattern of declining form figures (5-6-7-8-9) over varied surfaces does little to inspire confidence at this trip in this company.|
runners_data.comment: Jambearee has run over today's trip and was fifth last time, and carries 152 lb today, with our rating of 72 marking him out as a live threat in this field; the main concern is a lengthy 86-day absence leaving his fitness on trust.

runners_data.name: Lynxman
runners_data.note: Lightly campaigned on the Flat with no wins or places on similar going (0W0P in 2 soft-ground starts), and stepping into hurdles for Sowersby off 130 days; the jockey claim from Charlie Maggs (3) is an advantage in a race where weight matters, but his natural trailing instinct is squeezed into a midfield slot that does not suit Cartmel's shape.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Lynxman has had a significant break of 130 days since last seen and steps in carrying 152 lb, leaving plenty to discover about his potential.

runners_data.name: Time Twister
runners_data.note: Three runs in eight months for Easterby without a win or place on similar ground (0W0P, 1 similar-going run), and the 23-day turnaround at least confirms fitness; held up by inclination but drawn into midfield on the map by field composition — the horse needs a stronger gallop than Wicksey is likely to set to deliver a meaningful late run.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Time Twister steps into the unknown here carrying 152 lb after a 23-day absence, and with no public form to dissect, he remains an intriguing unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Watcha Snoop
runners_data.note: Carries a finishing fade flag and has posted nothing better than tenth in five Flat starts, with modest placings even when the pace has played into her hands (1W1P on similar going from 9 starts); stepping up in trip from sprint distances is a significant ask and Adam Nicol's 0/4 14-day record offers no trainer momentum.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to plenty of improvement on debut, Watcha Snoop steps into the unknown here but a 30-day freshener leaves him likely to strip fit, and connections will be hoping he makes a promising opening statement carrying 152 lb.

runners_data.name: Royal Baroness
runners_data.note: Has shaped with some promise placing third and fourth in her best Flat runs on soft or soft-adjacent ground (3/5 similar-going record), and Miss Becky Smith's 7lb claim softens the weight burden; a natural hold-up runner placed into midfield by field composition, she needs luck in running on this enclosed track to produce her best.|

races.paceDynamic: Wicksey is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no credible rival to press her from the outset, she should stride into an uncontested lead and control the tempo across Cartmel's tight, undulating 2m1f on Good To Soft ground. The pace is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching — a lone leader on soft ground rarely burns herself out — meaning the race will be run at a measured gallop that keeps the field compressed and denies true hold-up horses the gap they need to weave through late. Vietnorm, the only runner with a natural hold-up profile that is not redistributed, is the one horse positioned to deliver a genuine late challenge if Wicksey's lead is reeled in through the final hurdle. The race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile: with one honest pacer setting a controlled tempo and the rest of the field bunched behind, a horse who tracks Wicksey closely and quickens from second or third will be hardest to beat. Several horses including Time Twister, Royal Baroness, Lynxman, and Jambearee are genuine hold-up types forced into midfield on the map because the field holds more rear-ward runners than the race shape has room for at the back — none of them are likely to secure the rail-hugging, prominent berth that Cartmel's tight track rewards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wicksey Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey breaks cleanly and sets a measured gallop unchallenged through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Wicksey dictates the fractions, keeps rivals in a compressed bunch, and her jumping fluency through the hurdles allows her to maintain momentum into the straight; horses who track her closely through the race have first run on the closers. A prominent or tracking profile that can travel into the final two hurdles without burning out is almost impossible to beat in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey's lead proves more gruelling than expected on soft ground and she fades sharply after the last.
scenarios.body: The pace from the front on testing ground takes its toll, and a runner with enough stamina and tactical patience who has been travelling within herself through the race can pick up the pieces; Vietnorm, the only non-redistributed hold-up type, is best placed to benefit. Jambearee and Time Twister could also feature if they jump well from their bunched midfield positions, though their redistributed status means they may not find the clean run this scenario demands.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed midfield horse secures a better-than-expected position early and tracks Wicksey throughout.
scenarios.body: Cartmel's tight circuit can allow compact fields to bunch quickly after the first bend, gifting a well-placed midfiellder an unplanned prominent berth; if Royal Baroness or Time Twister land that position they travel into contention cheaply. The soft ground and flat final furlong favour a horse who has been conserving energy just off the pace rather than grinding from deep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates to be more testing than the Good To Soft official description and stamina becomes the dominant factor.
scenarios.body: Wicksey, already in front and controlling every element of the race, simply stays on most doggedly while the field behind her struggle to accelerate on the softer patches through the final bend; her jumping becomes an irreplaceable weapon when rivals cannot quicken. This scenario rewards class and jumping efficiency over raw speed and Vietnorm's hold-up profile is too far back to land a blow in time.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Wicksey jumps cleanly at the first two hurdles — any mistake early hands the pace initiative to a chasing pack that may raise the tempo and undermine her entire race plan.

Lynxman and Time Twister both carry redistributed hold-up profiles into a midfield slot; if they move for position early on Cartmel's tight first bend they could crowd Royal Baroness and Jambearee, causing a chain reaction of interference through the field.

Jambearee's repeated fading pattern and 86-day absence combined with a hold-up style not suited to this pace shape makes her a horse to watch for early signs of jumping hesitation — any mistakes could see her drop out of contention quickly on this compact track.

The going is reported Good To Soft across all Cartmel races today — if overnight rain has left soft patches on the back straight, Vietnorm's stamina profile (multiple wins at 16f on Good) becomes more relevant as rivals trained over shorter Flat trips encounter a new test.|

races.name: Campbell & Rowley Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Handmedownastar
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in fine form (won last time, placed twice before that on soft), Nick Scholfield's yard firing at 2/14 over the past fortnight; the 2m6f trip and Good to Soft ground are squarely within his comfort zone and Sean Bowen's booking is a major positive at 99 days off — the main danger from the prominent berth.
runners_data.comment: Handmedownastar arrives on the back of a win last time out, and has shown consistent placing form in recent starts, including a further win and a second earlier in the sequence; the chief concern is a 99-day absence under a hefty 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Skipper
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 42 days; a young apprentice (Shane Fenelon, 5lb) takes the ride and must navigate from the rear in a messy midfield — only one placed run from ten on similar going is a concern, though a win last time out suggests ability on a good day.
runners_data.comment: Fairlawn Skipper is an each-way contender carrying 161 lb, though the 42-day absence gives slight pause; he has run over today's trip and going, and that winning effort last time out suggests he arrives in form, offset by an unplaced return the run prior.

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up operator at 13 years old whose soft-ground placed record (3 from 15) is modest but consistent; headgear (p) suggests connections are looking to sharpen him up, and Nathan Moscrop keeps it simple, though age and the busy midfield make winning unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated by our assessors, Dinons has finished third on two of his last five starts and second on another, showing consistent competitiveness at this level; he carries a hefty 160 lb, and his latest eighth suggests he needs to bounce back from that disappointing effort.

runners_data.name: Belvedere Blast
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer fitted with a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, racing just 16 days after his last run; his form has been exclusively on Good or Good to Soft ground rather than Soft proper, and Oakley Brown (5lb claimer) has to find a way through from a rear position — modest win/place record at this level.
runners_data.comment: Belvedere Blast arrives on the back of a third three starts back and a second third four starts back, giving him a consistent placed thread in recent starts, and at 16 days between runs he comes here fresh enough under 160 lb with experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Ballyearl
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and key pace-setter for the entire race; won over 17f on Good to Soft so stamina at 2m6f is a legitimate question, and his recent form (P8 in last two) is poor, but he controls the tempo entirely — watch whether he weakens off the final bend rather than wins.
runners_data.comment: Ballyearl has a win among his last five starts but has struggled for consistency since, posting a pulled up and an eighth in his last two outings; he has going experience in his favour, though 158 lb is a stiff burden stepping back in here.

runners_data.name: Nottodaybobo
runners_data.note: Has won twice in recent form over 2m (20f) on Good ground and genuinely threatens if he can get close enough to the pace; the 2m6f trip is new territory and soft going produced only a third from nine attempts, so the stamina-and-ground combination is a real risk despite his current confidence.
runners_data.comment: Nottodaybobo shaped with promise when a winner two starts back and three starts back, though he was only second last time out after a 44-day break; going experience helps, but 158 lb is a stiff ask for a horse rated 105 officially.

runners_data.name: Rauzan
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true preference is to race from the rear; compressed into the midfield by weight of hold-up types in this field, his style fit is rated 0.90 and he is unlikely to get the space he needs — consistent placed form on Good ground but limited on Soft (2/15).
runners_data.comment: Rauzan rates among the chief threats here on a mark of 100, and our ratings suggest he holds strong claims as the second-ranked runner in the field; he has run over today's trip and going, and returns after 44 days off carrying 153 lb, though his winless recent spell is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Secret Secret
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Brian Hughes aboard and two career wins to his name; has run consistently at 2m2f–2m6f on Good ground and the 2-day turnaround is worth monitoring for freshness, though Moffatt runs a string of horses here and Hughes is a shrewd judge of pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Secret Secret faces a stiff task here; he does have experience over today's trip and going, but a return just two days ago and a burden of 150 lb make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Well Educated
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with an excellent placed record (four seconds in recent runs) who will struggle to find his natural rearward position in this crowded midfield; his form is almost entirely on Good or Good to Firm ground (5/15 on soft), so the ground itself may temper his finishing kick regardless of position.

runners_data.name: Enya
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a consistent placed profile at 2m–2m1f on Good and Soft ground; this is her first run at 2m6f so the stamina test is unproven, and a 113-day absence adds a fitness query, but the 7lb claimer Leah Noreci taking the ride keeps costs down and she has shown tenacity when placed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Enya also returns from a 113-day absence carrying 146 lb; she has run over today's going before, and her placed efforts show she competes honestly, but that is modest consolation here.

runners_data.name: Big Gypsy King
runners_data.note: Young (4yo) hold-up type whose hurdles form is limited to a single win over 2m1f on Good; his natural position at the rear is unavailable in this field shape (style fit 0.92) and his experience over this trip and ground is minimal — Ryan Mania's quality is an asset but the profile is against him.
runners_data.comment: Big Gypsy King has won once in her last five starts, that success one run back, but she rates second-bottom of our ratings among these rivals and a 42-day absence adds to the concern, making her hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Dusky Days
runners_data.note: Consistent but limited hold-up performer whose entire placed record (one place from 15 on soft) reflects a horse that rarely threatens; fitted with a visor and a very recent run (2 days ago), he is mapped out of his natural position and his form string (067868) tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Masterminding
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a respectable placed record (four places including two seconds), currently raced out of his natural rearward position in this crowded field (style fit 0.91); Charlie Maggs (3lb claimer) is the booking, and stamina looks solid at 2m6f, but he needs a more attritional scenario to emerge from the pack.

races.paceDynamic: Ballyearl is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival willing to challenge for the lead in this 13-runner field over 2m6f on Good To Soft ground at Cartmel, he is virtually guaranteed to dictate his own rhythm from the front without serious early pressure. Cartmel's tight, undulating circuit heavily favours horses who travel prominently and conserve energy through the turns, meaning a controlled, sustainable gallop set by Ballyearl will play directly into the hands of prominent-tracking types who can sit just off the pace and pounce. Handmedownastar, Secret Secret and Enya are the natural prominent horses best placed to exploit that position, while the redistribution note flags that Rauzan, Big Gypsy King, Well Educated, Dusky Days and Masterminding — all genuine hold-up types — are unlikely to secure their preferred rearward berth in a field this competitive for space. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can latch onto Ballyearl's uncontested lead and sustain their effort through the final climb, rather than true closers forced to cover ground from further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ballyearl Dictates, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyearl sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the race develops into a test of jumping and stamina from the front.
scenarios.body: Ballyearl controls the tempo on a circuit that rewards rail-hugging, accurate jumping and front-position efficiency, softening the ground-testing finale for those immediately behind him; prominent types like Handmedownastar and Secret Secret track the pace and have first run on the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyearl's lead creates a falsely steady early pace that sets up one of the tracking prominent runners to quicken past him approaching the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop benefits those who travel fluently in second or third, conserving stamina for the Cartmel hill; Handmedownastar's recent winning form and Enya's tenacious placed record in similar ground make them particularly dangerous off a soft pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Gains
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyearl goes too hard early on soft ground and weakens, opening the race up for horses who have been settled off the pace.
scenarios.body: A collapsing front-runner would theoretically benefit Nottodaybobo — a genuine winner in recent form — and Dinons, who has placed repeatedly on soft and stays well, though both must overcome the crowded midfield against redistributed hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Crowded Midfield Winner
scenarios.trigger: If there is interference, jumping errors or a bunched midfield scramble that disrupts the prominent horses and promotes a horse emerging late from the pack.
scenarios.body: With five redistributed hold-up horses compressed into the midfield, a chaotic race could produce a surprise from Masterminding or Well Educated — both of whom have consistent placed form — but the style-fit discounts make this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Ballyearl's stamina at 2m6f on soft is unproven — watch whether he begins to struggle jumping the final two hurdles after dictating throughout; if he weakens sharply, Handmedownastar and Secret Secret are perfectly positioned to capitalise.

Five hold-up horses (Rauzan, Big Gypsy King, Well Educated, Dusky Days, Masterminding) are all compressed into the midfield — watch for congestion and interference on Cartmel's tight bends in the early-to-middle stages, which could hamper multiple runners simultaneously.

Nottodaybobo is taking a significant step up in trip to 2m6f for the first time; if he weakens in the closing stages having raced prominently, he could cause traffic problems for those immediately behind him on the run-in.

Enya and Secret Secret both run for James Moffatt, who has four runners in this race — watch for any signs of in-stable tactics, particularly whether one horse is ridden to ensure a strong pace or to set it up for a stablemate.

Fairlawn Skipper won last time out and is the forgotten hold-up runner; if the midfield carnage opens a gap on the outside, Shane Fenelon (5lb) may find daylight at a big price — low probability but worth a visual note.

races.name: EWGA Handicap Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Al Sayah
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win and two places from four starts on similar going (soft/good-to-soft), running off 45 days freshened; Jack Tudor's booking suits and the 3m1½f trip has been handled before, making him a natural pace-tracking threat to Kayf Dancer.
runners_data.comment: Al Sayah landed a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 126 marking her a leading contender; the concern is a 45-day absence carrying 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Shallow River
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with two soft-ground wins in his last five, Sean D Bowen is a strong jockey booking, but 167 days since a competitive run is a concern and the 10-year-old's hold-up style requires more pace than Kayf Dancer is likely to supply.
runners_data.comment: Shallow River showed his class with a win four starts back and was back in the frame with a third two starts back, and carrying a hefty 168 lb is the one weight concern for a gelding our ratings put narrowly top of these rivals.

runners_data.name: Divilabother
runners_data.note: Arrives in red-hot form having won three of his last four, all on good ground — the step to soft here is the key question mark, though the trip suits and Harry Reed has ridden him consistently well; a prominent runner who should travel fluidly behind Kayf Dancer.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and carrying a hefty 167 lb, Divilabother is hard to fancy at the weights, though he has winning form in his last six starts and has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Imperial Merlin
runners_data.note: Long-absent (167 days) hold-up horse who handles soft ground well — his last win came on soft and four of five recent runs have been on that surface; Sean Quinlan is an accomplished claimer but the layoff is a significant risk factor at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Imperial Merlin catches the eye as a winner in his most recent completed start, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the concern is 167 days off the track, leaving fitness the key question for this threat.

runners_data.name: Kayf Dancer
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: sole front-runner who can dictate unchallenged at Cartmel, a notoriously tight and unforgiving track; soft-ground form is modest (0W2P from six starts) but his control of the pace is the dominant tactical fact of this race.
runners_data.comment: Kayf Dancer won two starts back but has since finished sixth, and 107 days off the track is a fitness query at this weight of 164 lb; he has experience of today's going, though his rating of 121 leaves him mid-pack in this field.

runners_data.name: Imperial Data
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by style whose recent form shows a fall, a pulled-up, and an eighth — the redistribution to midfield reflects overcrowding at the rear, meaning Richie McLernon may not get the patient ride that suits; form and fitness concerns compound the style mismatch.
runners_data.comment: Imperial Data has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 130 gives him a strong case as a leading threat at 161 lb, yet he arrives winless in recent starts and that fall last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Belles Benefit
runners_data.note: Won last time out on good ground and holds soft-ground form, but this closer-by-nature is unlikely to secure its preferred position at the back given the number of genuine hold-up rivals — Harry Bannister will need to adapt the ride, which dilutes the chance of the front-end staying power she needs to shine.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 149 lb, Belles Benefit is hard to fancy at the weights, though she does bring a third last time out and a win two starts back to the table, and has run over today's distance and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Kayf Dancer is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press from the flag in a seven-runner field over 3m1½f on soft ground at Cartmel, James Bowen can control this from the front at whatever tempo suits. Al Sayah and Divilabother are the two prominent types likely to track Kayf Dancer through the early stages, meaning the race will be run at a measured, sustainable pace with a clear pecking order established inside the first half-mile. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Imperial Data and Belles Benefit are genuine closers by nature but are shown in midfield because the shape leaves no true rear pocket for them; Shallow River and Imperial Merlin are the more authentic hold-up runners likely to occupy the back of the field. The soft going and extreme distance will stretch the field late, favouring horses that travel prominently and avoid cover issues — the tactical verdict is clear: the prominent-to-lead profile wins here, with Kayf Dancer's control and Al Sayah and Divilabother's jumping efficiency making them the dominant profile group.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kayf Dancer Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kayf Dancer sets a sustainable gallop from the front and the prominent pair Al Sayah and Divilabother fail to close the gap in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Kayf Dancer dictates every yard under James Bowen, the soft ground spreading the field and eliminating the closers' ability to produce a meaningful late challenge; horses tracking just off the pace in Al Sayah and Divilabother are best-placed to pick up any weakening winner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Al Sayah or Divilabother travel powerfully in Kayf Dancer's slipstream and produce superior stamina to reel him in over the final two flights.
scenarios.body: The soft ground and extreme trip expose any stamina limitation in Kayf Dancer, allowing Divilabother — whose recent hat-trick of wins shows peak form — or Al Sayah to collar him from a handy position; neither needs to produce a sprint finish, just sustained jumping fluency.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Stays On Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely hot enough to soften up the leaders and Shallow River or Imperial Merlin produce strong staying-on finishes from the rear.
scenarios.body: Shallow River has solid soft-ground form and Sean D Bowen's booking is significant, while Imperial Merlin landed a similar soft-ground opportunity last time; both need the front end to burn themselves out, which is possible but not the most likely shape given Kayf Dancer's one-paced front-running tendencies.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Hands Race To Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or jumping errors eliminate principals and the race falls apart structurally, opening the door for a horse racing out of role.
scenarios.body: Imperial Data and Belles Benefit, both natural hold-up types squeezed into midfield by race shape, would need a chaotic scenario to land this — their style fit is compromised at 0.92 and 0.93 respectively; this scenario is low-probability precisely because the dominant shape is clear and neither horse is racing in its true role.

watchPoints.text: Kayf Dancer jumping: at Cartmel's tight turns and with soft ground testing fluency, any blunder at a hurdle on the top bend could end his advantage in an instant — watch his jumping closely from flag fall.

Divilabother's going: all five recent starts have come on good ground and the step to soft today is unproven — if he struggles to travel on the softer surface, Al Sayah inherits the prominent role by default.

Imperial Merlin fitness: 167 days off is a lengthy break for a nine-year-old handicapper, and John & Sean Quinn's 3/16 strike rate in the last 14 days does not inspire confidence about a ready-to-run angle.

Shallow River market move: Olly Murphy's yard is in form (4/9 last 14 days) and Sean D Bowen is a significant jockey upgrade — any market support for this hold-up type would suggest connections expect more pace than the map projects.

Belles Benefit and Imperial Data in-running position: watch where McLernon and Bannister settle their horses in the first half-mile — if either is forced wide or too close to the pace, their redistributed-style issue will be immediately visible and their race is effectively over.

races.name: Wicks Group Cavendish Cup Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Grand Clermont
runners_data.note: Rock-solid recent form — two wins from five this season over similar trips on Good to Soft ground — and David Pipe's operation is quietly in form (T14: 1/10); Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim is a meaningful weight aid at 168lbs, and this horse's prominent style slots perfectly into the expected race shape here.|
runners_data.comment: Grand Clermont arrives on the back of a win one start back and a second last time out, bringing solid recent form into this; he carries a hefty 168 lb, which is the principal concern against this field.

runners_data.name: Breizh River
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's yard is in a sharp vein (T14: 3/9) and Breizh River has won over 2m1f and 2m4f on similar going; the step to 3m1½f is a query on breeding and form, though prominent racing on soft-leaning ground suits this type.|
runners_data.comment: Breizh River arrives here in excellent nick, a winner one start back and third last time out, with two wins from his last five starts and experience of today's going working in his favour; the main query is whether 44 days between runs leaves him short of peak sharpness under a hefty 167 lb.

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at OR 128 and carrying 164lbs with James Bowen aboard — a powerful combination — and the horse has won twice in recent outings including over 2m2f soft; the jump to 3m1½f is the key stamina question, though Mickey Bowen trains him well fresh (LR: 16d).|
runners_data.comment: Tamarind Bay unseated last time out, which tempers the enthusiasm somewhat, though he had won two of the three starts before that, most recently a winner two starts back and again three starts back. Has run over today's going and returns fit on a 16-day turnaround, but 164 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Tommie Beau
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old whose best form has come over 2m5f-3m on Good ground, and his true front-running instinct will be compromised here since faster horses are likely to push him wider and deeper than he wants; Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim helps at the weights but the race shape working against his natural style is a significant discount.|
runners_data.comment: Tommie Beau has mixed recent form, winning three starts back before a runner-up finish two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going. Carrying 163 lb after 44 days off is the one query, but his rating of 135 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Caughtinyourtrance
runners_data.note: Two wins on the bounce and Brian Hughes in the plate — this horse is confirmed going forward and has the course profile to lead uncontested at Cartmel; recent Good-to-Soft winning form stacks up well and James Moffatt's yard is ticking over (T14: 1/11), making him the key pace anchor for the whole field.|
runners_data.comment: Caughtinyourtrance arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, making him a serious player under 161 lb — the burden he carries is the one thing that could halt his momentum.

runners_data.name: Stratagem
runners_data.note: A dual course winner over 2m6f who naturally wants to race close to the pace, but with three prominent types ahead of him in the likely running order he will be shuffled back further than ideal; Mickey Bowen trains him well (T14: 4/18) and he is capable on his day, but his chance is genuinely tempered by racing at the back of his comfort zone.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Stratagem faces a stiff ask under 160 lb, yet he arrives with a lively recent profile — a winner last time out and two wins in his last five starts — and has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Flyer
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride for his father Mickey's yard and this is the only true hold-up horse in the field; three course wins in similar conditions and a strong place record (3W4P, sim-going) make him dangerous if the pace collapses late, though he will need significant fortune if the gallop remains controlled.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Fairlawn Flyer faces a stiff task here, though a pulled-up effort aside he has placed consistently and returns with distance and going experience to call on after 55 days off carrying 148 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Caughtinyourtrance is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Brian Hughes aboard, will dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over this stamina-sapping 3m1½f trip on Good To Soft ground at Cartmel. Grand Clermont, Breizh River, and Tamarind Bay are all genuine prominent racers who will push forward behind the leader, creating a compact early order with meaningful but not breakneck pace. This field contains more pace than the map can accommodate — Tommie Beau and Stratagem are natural prominent types redistributed to midfield on the map because they simply cannot all hold their preferred position; Grand Clermont and Breizh River, with stronger recent form and more convincing credentials at this trip, are best placed to actually secure those front ranks. The result is a race likely run at a controlled, honest clip that will reward horses who can travel close to the pace throughout and produce a genuine staying effort in the final mile — the prominent, pace-stalking profile is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Caughtinyourtrance leads at a sustainable tempo and the race is run to suit those travelling prominently throughout.
scenarios.body: Caughtinyourtrance sets a manageable gallop and the race becomes a test of stamina and jumping accuracy from the front rank, with the best-placed prominent traveller having first run from the second-last; horses carrying less weight and in good recent form at this trip thrive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Caughtinyourtrance jumps boldly, extends his lead on the final circuit, and the prominent pack cannot close.
scenarios.body: Hughes exploits a clear rail path at Cartmel and Caughtinyourtrance's recent back-to-back winning form to build an unassailable advantage jumping the last; at OR 125 and on good ground in a small field this is a live threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine prominent runners burn each other off through a faster early pace and the field strings out, leaving Fairlawn Flyer to stay on.
scenarios.body: Fairlawn Flyer has strong historical course and distance form (3W4P in similar conditions) and can pick up the pieces if those ahead tire; Sean Bowen's positional awareness gives this hold-up angle its best possible chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers, or unseated riders thin the field and create an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: With 18 fences over 3m1½f on softening ground, an incident-marred race could elevate any survivor regardless of style; Stratagem and Tommie Beau, pushed out of their natural prominent slot, might find traffic clears and drift into contention.

watchPoints.text: Caughtinyourtrance — if Brian Hughes jumps him smartly and establishes an uncontested lead within the first half mile, the race is almost certainly being run to his script; watch for him to be lobbing in front at the top of the hill.

Tamarind Bay and Tommie Beau — both want to race prominently and will compete with Grand Clermont and Breizh River for position behind the leader in the early stages; a scrappy, traffic-heavy opening mile could disadvantage all of them.

Stratagem — natural front-runner forced to race off the pace due to field composition; if he settles poorly or pulls hard from a rear position he will empty before the final fence regardless of ability.

Fairlawn Flyer — watch where Sean Bowen positions him at the start; if he is closer than his hold-up tag suggests he may be exploiting a small field, and that positional switch would significantly upgrade his chance in the run-in.

Going — the race-day report lists Good To Soft throughout Cartmel, slightly better than the "Soft" declared going; if the ground rides on the better end of Good To Soft it marginally helps Caughtinyourtrance and Grand Clermont whose form figures on similar conditions are strongest.

races.name: Fgh Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Pour Les Filles
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, trained by Mickey Bowen alongside stablemate King Roly; her ability to control the pace entirely unchallenged is her primary weapon, though a STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence that she can reproduce this at OR 127 over a trip she has yet to win at on softer ground.
runners_data.comment: Third on two of his last three completed starts, Pour Les Filles brings solid recent form to this contest and has run over today's trip and going before; winless in his last five starts, the 170 lb burden is the one query, but his rating of 137 marks him out as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Karnaval Point
runners_data.note: David Pipe's six-year-old arrives in fair form having won twice at 20f and 24f on Good ground; the step to 2m5f on a softer surface is the unknown, and a 5lb claiming rider aboard adds intrigue, but as the most likely horse to track the leader he is well placed tactically.
runners_data.comment: Karnaval Point boasts three wins in his last five starts, including a victory two runs back, and has run over today's trip, but that sixth last time out leaves a question mark over his current form after 36 days away carrying a hefty 168 lb.

runners_data.name: King Roly
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has recorded his best finishes on Good ground and carries the burden of a 12-day turnaround for the Bowen yard; his lone sim-going placing suggests softer conditions are not his optimum, and he will need a clean run through the pack to land a blow late.
runners_data.comment: King Roly arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while his our rating of 128 marks him out as a serious contender here; the main concern is a burden of 167 lb.

runners_data.name: Bleu d'Enfer
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's eight-year-old has placed twice on Good-to-Soft and softer, which makes him better-suited to today's conditions than several rivals; a genuine hold-up type who will need the pace to be strong enough to reel in Pour Les Filles, but his going record here is the most relevant positive flag.
runners_data.comment: Bleu d'Enfer has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 132 ranks him second in the field, marking him a leading contender despite carrying 167 lb; yet to score in his last five starts is the nagging concern.

runners_data.name: Cossack Chach
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature — his three-race winning sequence came over shorter trips on Good ground, and though redistributed to midfield on the map, he will trail the field in reality; the step up in trip and a 71-day absence may limit his ability to produce the necessary late surge.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win three starts back before pulling up two starts back, and his third last time out at least suggests some recovery — but 71 days on the sidelines and 164 lb to carry are notable tests of his readiness here.

runners_data.name: Sean Og
runners_data.note: Dianne Sayer's veteran has won twice at 21f on Good and has placed on Soft, making the trip and conditions acceptable; genuinely wired to sit last and pick off beaten horses, he will be held up in rear and needs the leaders to come back to him, which a slow pace makes unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Sean Og won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he has been off 44 days and his ranking of sixth of eight suggests he faces stiffer company than when successful; a stone-plus burden of 154 lb is no help either.

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: Six wins from his last six starts is a remarkable sequence, though all came on Good ground and his sole sim-going run was a fifth; Sam England's seven-year-old is a natural hold-up horse who thrives when the race sets up with a strong early pace — a sedate gallop is his biggest obstacle today.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of this field on our figures and carrying 153 lb after 44 days off, Passengerontheship is hard to fancy despite his remarkable run of five wins in his last six starts and experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Jack Sprat
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes rides this eight-year-old for James Moffatt on a handicap mark that looks competitive at OR 99; a hold-up type in practice who has shown placed form at Cartmel trips, but today's likely pedestrian pace off the front means he faces a stiff task getting from the back of the field to land a winning blow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Jack Sprat is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 142 lb; that said, he has placed in two of his three most recent outings and has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Pour Les Filles is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press from the front, she is set to control proceedings at a sustainable gallop through Cartmel's tight turns over 2m5f on Good to Soft ground. Karnaval Point is the most likely horse to track her prominently in second, with the remainder — King Roly, Bleu d'Enfer, Cossack Chach, Sean Og, Passengerontheship, and Jack Sprat — all natural hold-up or wait-and-pounce types who will be queuing up in the chasing pack. The field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Cossack Chach, Sean Og, Passengerontheship, and Jack Sprat are all true hold-up types redistributed forward on the map, and in reality they will trail the field, meaning the prominent berths behind Pour Les Filles are likely to fall to King Roly and Bleu d'Enfer rather than the nominal midfielders. An uncontested, sedate pace through the early stages on this tight track strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel kindly and produce a late surge, but with so many closers in the same group, the horse who can make the smoothest passage through the field and quicken soonest off the final bend will hold the decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pour Les Filles Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Les Filles is left entirely alone at the front and the hold-up pack leaves her undisturbed at a pace of her own choosing.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard, conserves energy through Cartmel's twists, and simply has too much left in reserve when the closers finally launch their challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Les Filles sets a genuinely dawdling pace that compresses the field, allowing the strongest hold-up horses to swoop in one move.
scenarios.body: The bunched-up finish suits a horse with strong late sectionals who can find a gap off the final turn; superior class and fitness off this trip becomes the differentiator.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Karnaval Point challenges Pour Les Filles earlier than expected and the two draw clear before the final fence.
scenarios.body: A pressured front two burn off the hold-up pack and the race becomes a match between the pair, rewarding class and jumping accuracy over the last two fences.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and a well-ridden hold-up horse threads through a gap to land a late sucker punch.
scenarios.body: Passengerontheship or Sean Og, both with strong recent winning form, could capitalise if traffic issues shuffle the prominent runners wide at the wrong moment.

watchPoints.text: Pour Les Filles controls all the pace and if the hold-up pack — Passengerontheship, Sean Og, Jack Sprat, Cossack Chach — fails to generate any pressure, she may simply trot up at her own tempo.

Karnaval Point ridden by a 5lb claimer (Rian Corcoran) represents a potential wild card — if the combination misjudges when to challenge Pour Les Filles, it could either inject unexpected pace or leave themselves flat at the last fence.

Bleu d'Enfer's two placed efforts on cut in the ground make him a genuine threat in Scenario B, but Cartmel's tight turning track can cause traffic problems for hold-up horses and Theo Gillard will need to manoeuvre early.

The Bowen yard runs two here (Pour Les Filles and King Roly); watch for any jockey instructions suggesting which is the yard's preferred runner, as Sean Bowen on the front-runner and James Bowen on the hold-up horse creates an interesting stable dynamic.

Going is reported Good to Soft for the 4:55 despite the race card showing Soft — if the track rides faster than expected, Pour Les Filles' stamina reserves are enhanced and the closers' finishing kicks may be less effective.

races.name: Furness Rda Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Ghasham
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Sam England with strong placed form over this trip on Good and Soft; six runs at similar going show no wins but three places, and a recent second 16 days ago over course-relevant trips keeps him fresh — needs the pace to be strong enough to reel in the leader from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Ghasham arrives on the back of a third last time out and a win four starts back, and has experience of today's trip and going; the weight of 168 lb is the one factor punters will watch closely.

runners_data.name: Achille Des Rocs
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter here, and with a clean lead on Good To Soft he sets the entire race shape; last five runs show modest form and limited experience in this going band (one run in eight), so his dominance of the pace map does not translate automatically into a winning chance — jumping accuracy at Cartmel's tight fences will be key.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field here and carrying 164 lb, Achille Des Rocs has run over today's trip and returns after a 40-day break that may have freshened him; the stark concern is three consecutive pulls-up in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Forcetoreckonwith
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes over on this Oliver Greenall/Josh Guerriero runner who has a solid record at 2m on Soft (one win, four places from six runs at this going type); 130 days off the track is the one concern, but the form profile before the break — 1-2-3-4 finishes — suggests a horse capable of running well fresh if fit.
runners_data.comment: Forcetoreckonwith showed plenty of ability when winning two starts back and was a close second three starts back, underlining her claims here, and she has experience on today's going; the chief concern is a 130-day absence since that fourth-place return.

runners_data.name: Cuzco Du Mathan
runners_data.note: James Moffatt's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up type by nature whose recent form (6-4-4-7-8) over 2m+ on Soft is modest; the 7lb claimer Leah Noreci rides, and the horse's three wins from 15 runs at similar going conditions show capability, but true hold-up horses will struggle to find their groove when several rivals are also angling for the same ground off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Cuzco Du Mathan has run over today's trip and going, returns after 44 days off, and our rating of 105 puts him second of these on the figures, though he'll need to find improvement on recent starts to end a winless run.

runners_data.name: Wearelongterm
runners_data.note: Dianne Sayer's nine-year-old prefers distance (best form over 3m+) and has always raced from the back, but the 2m1½f trip here is shorter than his optimum based on recent runs over 2m5f-2m6f; a genuine rear-of-field operator by instinct, his chance is further compromised by the number of similarly-styled rivals crowding the back of the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up among recent efforts, Wearelongterm is hard to fancy from a rating rank of seventh of eight; he has run over today's going before and 42 days between runs at least suggests he returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes partners this 12-year-old whose recent form of -2-3-2-2-1 over 2m-2m3f on Good is eyecatching and consistent, though all of that form has come on Good ground rather than Good To Soft; he is a natural finisher who has never won off similar going in 15 attempts (2 places), which is a significant flag when the ground could blunt his finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of eight on our figures, Getaway Jewel is hard to fancy despite a lively recent record that includes a win last time out and placed finishes in all five of his last starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 12 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: Raced just two days ago, which is an unusually tight turnaround and must be noted; the James Moffatt runner has a prominent style and his best effort in recent runs was a second over 2m6f at Goodwood, suggesting he may relish a stiffer test — five runs at similar going show one win and two places, and the prominent profile could see him sit ideally placed behind Achille Des Rocs.
runners_data.comment: Judicial Review has been winless in his last six starts, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; the concern is that he finished seventh last time out just two days ago, and carrying 147 lb tests his stamina despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Blazing Court
runners_data.note: John Dixon trains and his 7lb claimer son rides, bringing a distinct amateur angle; form reads -U-P-7-2-0 with the recent run being a non-finish, and both wins in his history have come at similar going, though the redistribution of his position away from the rear means he cannot fully exploit his natural patient style in this contested backmarker group.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and back out just two days after his latest unplaced effort, Blazing Court faces a quick turnaround; he has run over today's trip and going, and a second two starts back offers some encouragement, but 147 lb is a stiff ask.

races.paceDynamic: Achille Des Rocs is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner handicap chase over 2m1½f on Good To Soft ground at Cartmel, and with no genuine rival to press him for the lead, he is set to control the tempo from the front and dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Ghasham, Forcetoreckonwith, Cuzco Du Mathan, Wearelongterm, Getaway Jewel and Blazing Court all prefer to race from off the pace, while Judicial Review adds a prominent option — meaning the race is likely to be run at a measured clip through the early stages before the tempo lifts on the final circuit. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than can genuinely settle at the rear; Cuzco Du Mathan, Wearelongterm, Getaway Jewel and Blazing Court will all be competing for positions they cannot all occupy simultaneously, compromising the effectiveness of their preferred tactics. This race shape — a lone leader setting a controlled, honest pace over a stiff jumping track on soft-ish ground — strongly favours horses with the stamina to travel close enough to the pace before staying on powerfully in the straight, giving the edge to prominent-to-midfield types with proven form at this trip and on this going.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Achille Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Achille Des Rocs bowls into an uncontested lead and the hold-up horses fail to make meaningful headway off a steady early pace.
scenarios.body: Achille Des Rocs controls every yard at a tempo that suits him, jumping fluently and stretching clear from the second-last as the backmarkers have too much ground to make up on testing ground; horses who managed to race prominently or track closely will be best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If one or two prominent-tracking horses keep Achille Des Rocs honest through the middle stages and overhaul him on the run-in.
scenarios.body: A horse like Judicial Review or Forcetoreckonwith sits just behind the leader through the race, pouncing as Achille Des Rocs begins to tire after the last fence on ground that can stretch stamina reserves; the winner will likely be a durable stayer who has shown consistent placed form at this sort of trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Comes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring genuine finishers into play and one of the backmarkers produces a sustained staying run.
scenarios.body: A horse like Ghasham, whose hold-up profile and Good-to-Soft form figures suggest some ability to close late, delivers a sustained run from off the pace; given how congested the rear of the field will be with redistributed horses, only the cleanest jumper at pace is likely to get through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Achille Des Rocs jumps and travels so fluently that no rival gets into contention at any point and he wins going away.
scenarios.body: Despite soft going that might be expected to bring horses back to him, Achille Des Rocs proves superior in class and jumping accuracy, winning with something in hand; his near-absence of comparable course or going form makes this an unlikely outcome, but the race shape clearly sets up the possibility.

watchPoints.text: Achille Des Rocs jumps clean and dictates — if he pings the early fences at Cartmel and establishes even three lengths of daylight by the halfway point, no hold-up horse in this field has the natural pace to reel him back on Good To Soft ground.

Getaway Jewel's going record is a serious red flag — zero wins from 15 runs at Good To Soft or softer despite excellent recent form on Good ground; Brian Hughes will need to be positive early to counteract the ground concern, making his positioning in the first mile critical to watch.

Judicial Review ran just two days ago; if he shows any sign of staleness or unwillingness to settle in the early stages, Callum Bewley may be forced to drop him out rather than press, fundamentally changing the race's prominent section dynamic.

The cluster of hold-up types — Ghasham, Cuzco Du Mathan, Wearelongterm, Getaway Jewel and Blazing Court — all seeking the same ground at the rear means jumping errors in the chasing pack could cause serious interference; monitor the first three fences to see which horse actually secures clean cover and which is forced wider than ideal.
